title: Intuition and assumptions
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you spend your time on when you have a new idea: the numbers, or the assumptions?

I said that this call I wanted to ask questions that are a little rhetorical, and asked everyone to write them down. These are hard, compromising questions, but important not to lie to ourselves about: what are we deciding to do with our lives?

I gave an example from the person in the book: humans drive using visual data, so our cars should use visual data, instead of the engineers who say they should use sensors. I called that intuition beginning.

When you are about to turn an idea into a business, I asked, what empowers your intuition? Assumptions in a business drive the financials. A lot of people make wonderful spreadsheets, but I spend seventy percent of my time on the assumptions, then I go to the numbers.

A student described their process: research the topic, brainstorm innovations around it, ask different questions from the researchers' first questions, then look at the research and make their own assumptions.

I asked another student for their personal limitations in that process. They said: it's okay not to have all the answers. The limitation is experience, because I'm just doing the research, not the actual hands-on work.
A student said another limitation is trying to follow cold, hard technical data, because intuition is a little off the wall and isn't easily justifiable to experts.
I said: that is very relevant. The engineers have the data and say: you are outside of reality, we have no data. One limitation is: I have no data, therefore it's not reality.
What are your assumptions, and how many hours have you given them?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the idea you are working on.
Write what evidence you have for each.
Write the limit that holds your intuition back.
Write how much time you will give the assumptions before the numbers.

check.q: What did I say assumptions in a business drive?
How much of my time did I say I spend on assumptions?
What limitation did a student name about intuition?
choices: It is hard to justify to experts who follow the data

recap: Study your assumptions before your numbers. Know the limits on your intuition.
